town-green-civic.prompt: The civic heart of the Crossing: an old, busy lowland trade town opening around public green or stone square, mixed timber-and-stone frontage visibly worn by daily use, practical paths and gathering space. Preserve grass, fountain, monument, market activity, or civic details only when named by the room; no palace scale, no pristine empty plaza, no invented magical spectacle.

market-commercial.prompt: Dense commercial streets of the Crossing, a working lowland trade town: close mixed timber-and-stone shopfronts, canvas awnings, pedestrian traffic and practical wear. Goods, carts, signs and crowd density must vary with the source room; no modern storefronts, no grand capital-city avenue, no universal river or temple details.

river-quays.prompt: The Crossing's working river edge where the room text establishes water: Segoltha-facing quays, timber landings or stone embankment, damp wear and a practical trade-town skyline. Boats, rope, cargo, bridge structure and crowds appear only when supported; water must dominate the geography, and the scene must not read as an inland street or ocean harbor.

gates-walls.prompt: Practical defensive perimeter of the Crossing: fortified town wall and working gate approaches at human town scale, mixed masonry and timber repairs, clear inside/outside orientation. Traffic, guards and surrounding vegetation depend on the room text; no giant castle, mountain citadel, palace gate or invented siege.

temple-quarter.prompt: Quieter ceremonial approaches in the Crossing temple quarter, with cleaner sightlines and the town's worn mixed construction. Religious architecture, gardens, water, statuary and artificial light appear only when established by the specific room; no generic cathedral, glowing magic or single-faith iconography imposed across the quarter.

residential-backstreets.prompt: Narrow irregular lanes and lived-in backstreets of the Crossing, enclosed by worn practical timber-and-stone buildings with restrained trade-town clutter. Keep each route readable and vary prosperity according to room text; do not turn every alley into a criminal slum, sewer, night scene or torch-lit menace.

riverpine-outskirts.prompt: The greener edge of the Crossing where dense settlement thins into lowland road, trees and open ground. Let vegetation and route geometry dominate while distant town fabric appears only when supported; no dense market street, no deep untouched wilderness, and no forced river view.

amusement-carousel.prompt: The distinctive amusement and carousel complex of the Crossing, an ornate but weathered public entertainment space with stronger color and crafted decoration than ordinary streets. Carousel machinery, pier water, booths, crowds and interiors must follow the named room; no modern carnival technology, electric lighting or generic market-street substitution.

forcing river, temple, market or fortification details into unrelated rooms
